description:
Hypothesis (cannot confirm without writing a probe; this review is read-only):

CalendarEvent.ical_component has '#[serde(rename = "iCalComponent")]' (src/event.rs:111). The doc explicitly mentions that the spec wire name is 'iCalComponent' (capital I, capital C in 'Cal'), and the camelCase rename_all derivation would naturally produce 'icalComponent' (lowercase i). A peer that follows 'obvious' camelCase rules produces 'icalComponent' on the wire. When such a CalendarEvent is deserialized:

  - The typed ical_component field will not match (only 'iCalComponent' matches).
  - The CalendarEvent.extra catch-all (#[serde(flatten)], src/event.rs:301) WILL capture it.
  - The typed .ical_component will be None even though the data was present on the wire.
  - On re-serialize, 'icalComponent' is preserved in .extra and re-emitted, preserving the bug.

Trigger condition: any peer implementation that capitalizes 'iCal' as a brand differently than the spec — Apple's own iCalendar tooling, third-party calendar exporters, naive code-gen.

Probe required (NOT performed in this read-only review):
  let json = r#"{"id":"e1","icalComponent":"BEGIN:VEVENT...END:VEVENT"}"#;
  let ev: CalendarEvent = serde_json::from_str(json).unwrap();
  assert!(ev.ical_component.is_none(),    "typed field should be None");
  assert!(ev.extra.contains_key("icalComponent"), "should leak into extras");

Why not confirmable by reading: serde's #[serde(flatten)] resolution rules around field renames are conservative and would consume 'icalComponent' only if rename_all were strict camelCase on this field. Because the explicit #[serde(rename)] overrides, 'icalComponent' likely falls through to the flatten catch-all. Probe needed to confirm.

If confirmed: file as a P1 finding (silent data loss for non-conformant peers). Possible mitigations: add a deserialize alias for 'icalComponent' that warns; or do nothing and document the brand-mismatch hazard in Gotchas.

File path: crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/event.rs:101-113
title: calendars-types: probe — does 'icalComponent' (naive camelCase) leak into CalendarEvent.extra?
